newsitem.title: UK: Mideast dirty tankers steady, Caribs fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: Mideast dirty tankers steady, Caribs fall sharply.

text.p: Middle East dirty tanker rates were steady to slightly firmer on Tuesday in quiet activity due to the Chinese new year and Moslem holidays, brokers said.
One broker said there was scope for very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates to rise by the end of the week or early next.
"Stems are allocated from the Middle East around mid-month. On Friday/Monday/Tuesday we could see some heavy demand from the Japanese," he added.
Mideast/West VLCCs were fixed at W50/52.5, up to 2.5 points higher, with trips to Japan steady at W65 and to Singapore at W50.
The sharpest fall was seen in the Caribbean, with 70,000 tonne Caribs/upcoast down some 15-20 points at W115-120 on a lack of enquiry and with five or six prompt ships available, a U.S. broker said.
Caribs/U.S. 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were steady at W170.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs remained strong at W67.5, up five points from late January, with 130,000 tonne cargoes at W90, brokers said.
The North Sea/U.S. sector was inactive, with brokers continuing to assess VLCCs at about W65 and 130,000 tonne ships at W90.
In the Mediterranean, 80,000 tonne cargoes slipped to W120 from W125, continuing their fall after spiking up to W170 last month.
"There are less and less cargoes and a lot of vessels. If this continues it could drop more," an Italian broker said.
Med 130,000 tonners were quiet at around W92.5, while inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne cargoes were likewise little changed at W95-100.

Cross-Med fuel oil firmed to W205-210 for 25,000 tonnes on a good quality ship, or around W190 for an elderly ship, with inter-U.K./Cont down to W205 from W210, one broker said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
